speaker: Doctor
text: How high has your fever reached, and does the pain in your side worsen when you press on the area? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Leukocyturia: Present, Bacterial_Culture: Negative, Cytospin_Stained_With_Hansel’s_Solution: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm

speaker: Doctor
text: That finding of eosinophilic cells is unusual and might suggest an allergic reaction to the recent antibiotic rather than a typical bacterial infection. Do you have a history of allergies, and did you develop a rash after starting the medication? REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal liver tests and the presence of eosinophilic cells, I need to clarify the nature of the flank pain. Does the pain radiate toward your groin, and do you notice any changes in your urine color or frequency? REQUEST TEST: Renal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal ultrasound effectively rules out kidney stones or obstruction, and with normal liver function, the eosinophilic cells on your urine stain strongly suggest an interstitial nephritis caused by the recent antibiotic. Are you experiencing joint pain or a rash, which are common accompanying symptoms for this condition? DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyelonephritis
